fixed.explanation: resolveGlobBase replaces every path token, including host:port, with an opaque placeholder. That stops URL normalization of default ports, percent-encoding and punycode. The fix replaces only tokens that contain glob special characters (*, ?, {, }, backslash). Literal tokens go through URL resolution unchanged.

query.intent: URL glob-to-regex conversion and base-URL resolution of glob patterns replaces every part of the URL (host, port, path) with an opaque placeholder before calling the URL constructor, so normalization of default ports, percent-encoding and punycode is lost. Should only replace parts containing glob special characters (*, ?, {, }, backslash) with placeholders and leave literal parts to URL resolution.
query.symptom: A URL glob pattern with an explicit default port (e.g. http://localhost:80/**), a space, or an IDN host never matches the normalized request URL in route, waitForURL and toHaveURL.
